UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                      BEFORE THE
                        FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


                                                 )
    Midcontinent Independent System              )                 Docket No. ER27-25-000
    Operator, Inc.                               )


                          MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS OF
                                  BASE ELECTRON, CORP.

           Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC”

or the “Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure,1 and the Commission’s October 2, 2026

Notice regarding the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.’s (“MISO”) proposed

revisions to its Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff (“Tariff”)

to implement the Large Load Addition Resource Study (“LARS”), Base Electron, Corp. (“Base

Electron”) respectfully submits this Motion to Intervene and Comments.

      I.       MOTION TO INTERVENE

           Base Electron, an independent power producer, respectfully moves under Rules 212 and

214 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure2 to intervene in this proceeding. Base

Electron and its subsidiaries are developing a portfolio of dedicated, dispatchable power projects

designed to provide large-load customers, including hyperscale data center operators, and artificial

intelligence and advanced computing companies, with access to firm, reliable, cost-efficient, grid-

connected power at scale. Base Electron supports the initiatives undertaken by MISO to develop

LARS and implement it in its Tariff. Moreover, Base Electron participated in MISO’s stakeholder

process that preceded MISO’s filing in this docket. As provided below, Base Electron seeks to

    18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212, 385.214.
2

 intervene in this proceeding to offer limited comments on items within MISO’s proposal where

clarification and confirmation would be beneficial for entities seeking to interconnect under the

LARS procedures.

          Given its planned development in MISO, Base Electron has a direct and substantial interest

in proposed revisions to MISO’s Tariff, such as those related to LARS. Therefore, Base Electron’s

interests may be directly affected by the outcome of this proceeding and cannot adequately be

represented by any other party. Accordingly, Base Electron respectfully requests that the

Commission grant this timely motion to intervene with full rights associated with party status in

this proceeding.

   III.      COMMENTS

          At the outset, Base Electron supports timely acceptance of MISO’s LARS Tariff proposal.

Base Electron’s comments neither seek to delay the resolution of this proceeding nor request FERC

to condition or delay effectiveness of MISO’s LARS proposal on the requested clarification and

confirmation herein.




                                                  2
         Base Electron’s comments seek clarification and confirmation on a single item within

MISO’s proposal: for the purpose of determining the allowable Interconnection Service amount

requested under the LARS Interconnection Request, whether the LARS Associated Load’s

“expected peak Demand” means the load’s Demand at the time it first takes service or the expected

peak Demand once any planned future phase build-outs of the load are in service.3 Put differently,

how will MISO measure the LARS Associated Load’s expected peak Demand?

        MISO’s proposed Tariff revisions implementing LARS provide that “[a]n Interconnection

Request seeking LARS processing shall request NRIS Interconnection Service in an amount that

is both: (1) not less than 200 MW, and (2) not more than 150% of the peak Demand of the LARS

Associated Load.”4 Moreover, the proposed Tariff revisions later state that the Interconnection

Service requested “must not exceed 150 percent of the LARS Associated Load’s expected peak

Demand.”5 In further support of the need for clarification, MISO states that a LARS Associated

Load can come online in phases and that “[t]he LARS Application should identify the total

expected large load amount that is aligned with the full Generator Interconnection Service request

not to exceed 150% of the peak demand of the LARS Associated Load.”6

        Base Electron’s comments merely seek clarification and confirmation on how and based

on what parameters MISO will measure the 150% limit on Interconnection Service for the

interconnecting generator, when a LARS Associated Load might commence service in phases (i.e.,

how MISO will measure expected peak Demand). As Base Electron understands it, the 150% cap

on Interconnection Service is not measured on any first or initial phase of the load, but on a total




3
  MISO, Proposed Tariff, Attachment X (193.0.0), § 3.12.2; id., § 1 (Definitions).
4
  Id., Attachment X (193.0.0), § 3.12.2.vi.

6

Oct. 2, 2026) (Drake Test.).

                                                       3
 expected load at the conclusion of any phases anticipated by the LARS Associated Load.

Clarification and confirmation from MISO on this issue is important because, according to the

LARS Tariff proposal, a generator cannot change requested Interconnection Service after the

submission of the LARS Application and prior to the execution or unexecuted filing of the final

Large Load Generator Interconnection Agreement.7 Likewise, MISO’s testimony states that for the

LARS Associated Load, “[a]ny increase in the amount of load demanded is not allowed and the

customer would need to submit a new LARS Application or apply for some other kind of

Interconnection Service.”8 If the 150% limit on Interconnection Service is measured by a load’s

first phase, and not the expected and anticipated future load size, the interconnecting generator

would be precluded from adequately sizing its facility to meet the full load at final phased build-

out. In turn, any remaining generator Interconnection Service to serve a full build-out of the load

could then be required to go through MISO’s Definitive Planning Phase process, which includes a

longer study timeline.

        In conclusion, Base Electron respectfully requests confirmation and clarification on (1)

whether “expected peak Demand” for purposes of deriving the 150% limit on Interconnection

Service requested by the generator means the LARS Associated Load’s expected peak once it

“commence[s] service for the full amount of transmission service requested in the LARS

Application”;9 and (2) whether a LARS Interconnection Request that sizes its Interconnection

Service based on the load’s full expected peak measured by future anticipated phases satisfies

Attachment X, § 3.12.2.vi, even if the LARS Associated Load initially takes service at a lower

level during any preliminary phase build-out.

    IV.      CONCLUSION

         For the foregoing reasons, Base Electron respectfully requests that its motion to intervene

be granted by the Commission, and the preceding comments be considered by the Commission in

its review of MISO’s filing in this proceeding. Base Electron reiterates that its comments merely

seek clarification and confirmation, which could be provided either in any MISO answer it may

file or in FERC’s order in this proceeding, and it neither seeks to delay the resolution of this

proceeding nor requests FERC to condition or delay effectiveness of MISO’s LARS proposal on

the requested clarification and confirmation herein.
